advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify in AGENTS.md and mcp-auth.md §7 that the require_environment/opcert_enforce_since flip enforces only the completion-verifier op-cert kind (plan-review is gated separately), per ADR 0104.
evidence: docs/mcp-auth.md:299-304: 'The two op-cert kinds minted via MCP — plan-review (claim) and completion-verifier (close) — ... So a cert minted through MCP is enforceable-when-enabled via that trusted environment.'

AGENTS.md:137-139: 'Routed through the on-box MCP server they are signed under the box’s registered trusted signing environment, so a project can enforce that a certified op was produced there. That enforcement is enableable but currently deferred...'

docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md:120-129: 'verify-opcert enforces only the completion-verifier op-cert kind ... Plan-review certs are minted under the same environment but are gated separately (they are not the require_environment lane).'
advisory.finding: Both AGENTS.md and mcp-auth.md §7 describe the operator flip (verify.require_environment + verify.opcert_enforce_since) as enabling enforcement of 'a certified op' / 'the two op-cert kinds' generically, but ADR 0104 states that flip enforces ONLY the completion-verifier kind and that plan-review certs are gated separately (not the require_environment lane). The generic wording could mislead an operator into believing one flip enforces both op-cert kinds.

coverage.approach_viability_note: 0 surviving high-priority finding(s), Pass-2 drop-rate 67% — the approach (not just nits) may be worth a second look (advisory; the verdict is unchanged).

evidence: New §7: `location /mcp/ {` with `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp;` and comment `# external https://<box>/mcp/  →  loopback app http_path /mcp`
§5 reference recipe (docs/mcp-auth.md:200-201): `location /mcp {` / `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000;` (URI-less, preserves full path)
nginx semantics: a proxy_pass with a URI replaces the location-matched prefix, so `location /mcp/` + `proxy_pass .../mcp` yields `/mcp` for `/mcp/` and `/mcp<suffix>` for `/mcp/<suffix>`
dropped.finding: The new §7 nginx recipe uses `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp;` under `location /mcp/`. Because this proxy_pass carries a URI, nginx replaces the matched `/mcp/` prefix with `/mcp`, so `/mcp/` proxies to `/mcp` (trailing slash dropped) and any subpath `/mcp/<x>` proxies to `/mcp<x>` (e.g. `/mcp/messages` -> `/mcpmessages`), not `/mcp/messages`. The §5 reference recipe deliberately uses a URI-less `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000;` which preserves the full request path. The §7 comment claiming the edge maps `/mcp/` -> app `/mcp` is misleading and the recipe likely mis-routes subpaths.
dropped.suggested_fix: Match the §5 pattern: either use `location /mcp/ { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp/; }` (both trailing slashes, so `/mcp/<x>` -> `/mcp/<x>`) or a URI-less `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000;` with the app path aligned; and correct the mapping comment accordingly.

evidence: New §7 toml sets `http_host = "127.0.0.1"` and `http_path = "/mcp"` but no `http_port`
§1 (docs/mcp-auth.md:23) documents `http_port = 8000` as the default the recipe implicitly depends on
dropped.finding: The §7 `[tool.rebar.mcp]` config block sets `http_host` but omits `http_port`, while the accompanying nginx block hardcodes `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000...`. The recipe silently relies on the default port (8000, documented only in §1) being unchanged; a reader who sets a different `http_port` will have an nginx target that no longer matches, with nothing in §7 flagging the coupling.
